Comparison

Best services for booking meetings at SaaS conferences

By Or Alperovitz, founder of A8Z · Updated November 5, 2026

Short answer: If you want a team to run pre-event outreach and book the meetings for you, compare A8Z, ExpoToFunnel, Profitable Events and Skylarq. If your own team will run the outreach and you need event and contact data, look at a tool like Lensmor. If events are one part of a wider marketing program, a broader agency like SeeResponse may fit better.

Disclosure: A8Z wrote this comparison and is one of the companies in it, so read it with that in mind. It's listed alphabetically, not ranked. Details come from each company's own website as of November 5, 2026, and we haven't tested these competitors ourselves. Please confirm details with each company directly.

Side-by-side comparison

CompanyTypeWho does the outreachConsider it for
A8ZOutbound agencyA8Z's teamEnd-to-end event outreach by email, LinkedIn and phone, plus ongoing outbound between events
ExpoToFunnelTrade show ranking plus booking serviceExpoToFunnel's teamChoosing which shows to attend, then getting meetings and per-meeting briefs
LensmorEvent intelligence softwareYour teamFinding events, exhibitors, likely attendees and contact details
Profitable EventsPre-event outreach specialistThe consultant behind the serviceA focused email and LinkedIn campaign around a large show
SeeResponseB2B marketing agency with an event practiceSeeResponse's teamEvent promotion and follow-up as part of wider marketing
SkylarqAI agents plus an outreach teamSkylarq's team, with your approvalEvent planning, booked meetings, hosted dinners and pipeline tracking

How we compared them

  • Who does the work: does the company run outreach for you, or give you data to use yourself?
  • Channels: which channels does it say it uses to reach attendees?
  • Scope: does it cover event selection, booking and follow-up, or only part of that?
  • Fit for a small team: can it work for vendors without their own SDR team?

We didn't compare meeting counts or results, because companies report them differently and we can't verify them.

The options

A8Z

A8Z is our own agency. We run outbound end to end, and book meetings at SaaS conferences and other tech events through email, LinkedIn and phone, followed by post-event follow-up. We have booked 500+ meetings with technical buyers across our work. It's a good fit if you want the same team to handle events and ongoing outbound, or if you sell to technical buyers. Look elsewhere if you want software you run yourself, or a partner to host your event dinners.

ExpoToFunnel

ExpoToFunnel offers a free ranking of trade shows based on your ideal customer profile. Its team then matches attendees on buying signals, books meetings and writes a brief for each one. It's worth a look if you haven't decided which shows to attend.

Lensmor

Lensmor is software for finding trade shows, exhibitors and likely attendees that match your ideal customer profile, with contact enrichment and integrations. It's built for teams that will run their own outreach, so you'll need people to do that work.

Profitable Events

Profitable Events is a pre-event outreach service written in the first person by the consultant who runs it. It covers data work, email and LinkedIn outreach, reply handling, booking and post-event follow-up, and it focuses on large shows with 5,000+ attendees. Its site lists campaigns for events including Web Summit, Slush and VivaTech.

SeeResponse

SeeResponse is a broader B2B marketing agency with an event marketing practice for companies that host, sponsor or exhibit. It focuses on getting the right accounts to attend, and on follow-up that creates pipeline. It makes the most sense if you want events tied to your wider marketing.

Skylarq

Skylarq pairs AI agents that research events with a team that does the outreach, books meetings and hosts dinners, and it tracks results in your CRM. It's aimed at founders, field marketers and sales teams, and it's worth a look if you run a full event calendar and want planning and measurement in one place.

How to choose

  • No SDR team? Choose a service that runs the outreach and handles replies.
  • Already have SDRs? An event data tool may be enough.
  • Not sure which events to attend? Look for help with event selection first.
  • Want pipeline beyond events? Choose a partner that can also run ongoing outbound.

Questions to ask before you hire anyone

  • How do you count a meeting: booked, or actually held?
  • What makes a meeting qualified, and who decides?
  • How do you find out who is really attending?
  • Which channels will you use, and do we approve messages first?
  • Have you worked this event or sold to our buyers before? Can we speak to a reference?
  • What happens after the event?

Starting early matters whichever option you choose. Read our guide on how to book meetings before a trade show or conference.
